sections.h2: How does selling a house in North Huntingdon work?
sections.html:
North Huntingdon sellers deal with a township, a county and a school district that each tax and record separately, and the township's permit schedule lists no resale inspection for an ordinary house. North Huntingdon is a first class township in Westmoreland County covering about 27 square miles, governed by a board of commissioners with one commissioner from each of seven wards.

Census QuickFacts counts 31,880 residents in 2020 and 31,697 in its 2025 estimate. The township is crossed by the Pennsylvania Turnpike (I-76) and the Lincoln Highway (U.S. Route 30), with the Youghiogheny River touching its southwestern corner, as described on Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What are North Huntingdon's housing and neighborhoods like?
sections.html:
North Huntingdon is mostly a township of owner-occupied houses, with 90.1 percent of housing units owner occupied in the 2020 to 2024 Census figures. The survey puts a typical owned home at $232,400, household income at $101,200 at the median, and 94.4 percent of residents at the address they occupied the prior year.

Older sections of the township grew around settlements such as Circleville, Cavitt's Mills and Robbin's Station, and the Fullerton Inn and the McFarlane House carry federal historic register listings. Students attend the Norwin School District.

About 21.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, so estate sales and downsizing moves are part of the local picture. QuickFacts also reports about $826 million in retail sales for 2022.

sections.h2: Does North Huntingdon require an inspection before a house sale?
sections.html:
The township's permit fee schedule lists a residential occupancy permit for new construction only, at $25 and included in the building permit fee, which means an existing owner-occupied house changing hands does not go through an occupancy inspection. Commercial occupancy for a new use or tenant costs $150.

Permits still matter for projects a seller finishes before listing:

  • Residential building permits are charged per square foot plus a state fee and review fee, and the application will not be accepted without a property survey.
  • Accessory buildings under 200 square feet skip the building permit but need a $50 zoning permit.
  • Demolition requires proof of utility shut-offs, and the township inspector checks the sewer cap before backfilling.
  • Inside and outside sanitary sewer inspections on permitted construction are handled by the North Huntingdon Township Municipal Authority.

The Planning and Zoning Department takes questions at 724-863-3806, extension 220, and inspections need 24 hours of notice.

sections.h2: How is North Huntingdon property tax calculated?
sections.html:
The tax bill multiplies the Westmoreland County assessed value, divided by 1,000, by each millage rate, and three bodies levy: the township, the county and the Norwin School District. The township's 2026 budget document describes a general real estate rate of 10.73 mills, up from 9.23, and uses a $24,000 assessed value as the median household example.

The same document drops the per capita tax and adds a 2.0 mill increase for the capital reserve fund. Confirm the adopted figures on your own bill, since the budget file is labeled proposed.

Since August 1, 2024, Keystone Collections Group has collected the township's occupation tax, local services tax and delinquent real estate tax, and Norwin School District sends its own separate bill. The township tax office on Center Highway handles current township real estate bills.

sections.h2: How do Westmoreland County assessment appeals work?
sections.html:
An owner can appeal an assessment to the Westmoreland County Board of Assessment Appeals every year, and annual appeals must be filed on or before August 1 to take effect for the following tax year. Anyone who receives a notice of change in assessment has 40 days from the mailing date to appeal.

Appeal forms are posted in the Forms section of the county site and are available from the Tax Assessment Office at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue in Greensburg. The board meets on the second Thursday of each month at 9:00 a.m. in the Tax Assessment Office, Suite 440.

Because the township uses county values, a successful appeal changes the township and school bills together. A seller who plans to list should file before the August 1 deadline if the assessed value looks high compared with similar houses nearby.

sections.h2: What recording and transfer tax steps apply in North Huntingdon?
sections.html:
A deed for a North Huntingdon house is recorded with the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds, which requires the 10-digit parcel identifier number on every document. The recorder's list also calls for original signatures, a certified grantee address, and either transfer taxes or a completed Statement of Value (REV-183) unless a family exemption appears in the deed.

The state portion is 1 percent of the value transferred, and the state revenue agency notes that grantor and grantee are jointly liable. The township's 2026 budget lists real estate transfer tax revenue of $650,000, which shows a local share applies as well, so ask the Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate on your parcel.

If a deed's transfer tax covers more than one municipality, it must state how the tax is divided.

sections.h2: How are North Huntingdon's roads, fire protection and utilities arranged?
sections.html:
The township's fire levy is shared equally among the seven volunteer fire companies inside its borders, and a separate hydrant levy applies only within 600 feet of a hydrant. The fire service line appears on every tax bill.

Wikipedia puts the township's road network at about 125 miles, and the 2026 budget message names roads and stormwater as its main spending emphasis. Sanitary sewer service and inspections run through the North Huntingdon Township Municipal Authority, which a seller can contact about a lateral line before a buyer's inspector raises it.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a North Huntingdon house?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits owners who need certainty on timing or who would rather not spend on updates before a buyer's inspection. A cash buyer purchases as is, which fits several common situations:

  • A long-held house that needs a new roof, furnace or sewer line.
  • An inherited property that heirs live far from.
  • A home with delinquent township, county or school taxes that moved to a collector.
  • A landlord who wants out of a rental on a short schedule.

Compare any offer with a likely net from a traditional listing, after agent fees, repairs and the transfer tax, and ask for a copy of the purchase terms before agreeing to anything.

faqs.q: Does North Huntingdon require a resale occupancy permit?
faqs.a: The township's fee schedule lists a residential occupancy permit for new construction only, so an ordinary resale of an existing house is not covered by it. Call the Planning and Zoning Department at 724-863-3806, extension 220, to confirm for your address.

faqs.q: What is the North Huntingdon real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The township's budget document shows a general real estate rate of 9.23 mills for 2025 and 10.73 mills for 2026, plus 1.32 mills for fire service. Westmoreland County and the Norwin School District tax the parcel separately, so check your bill for the full total.

Keystone Collections Group collects the township's occupation, local services and delinquent real estate taxes, and its phone number is 724-978-0300. Norwin School District bills its school taxes separately.

faqs.q: By what date must a Westmoreland County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Annual appeals must be filed on or before August 1 and take effect for the next tax year. A notice of change in assessment gives the owner 40 days from the mailing date to appeal.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax when selling in North Huntingdon?
faqs.a: Pennsylvania charges 1 percent at the state level, and local shares are added on top. The Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds can give the combined rate for your parcel before you sign a sales agreement.
